author: Codex socialist_green assessment agent (AI-assisted independent assessment)
changeNote: Completed 240 individually interpreted responses and separate substantive evidence review. User authorised neutral representative doctrinal modelling; no 12Axes answers or scores imported.

metadata.name: Christian Democracy (European social-market tradition)
metadata.description: European Christian democracy combining personal dignity, democratic pluralism, social-market economics and subsidiarity.
metadata.period: Post-war European tradition; 2012 EPP principles with 2025–2026 context
metadata.scope: Christian personalist, pluralist and subsidiarity-based European Christian democracy. EPP contemporary positions inform applications but do not make every EPP coalition decision doctrine; Catholic teaching is intellectual context rather than a clerical veto. This is a representative interpretation, not a questionnaire submitted by adherents. Numeric neutral means a stated mixed/conditional judgement, including rejection of the premise where explained; it is not a claim of measured empirical equivalence. Modern biological and technology items are conditional interpretive judgements where no exact historical position exists; they must not be read as empirical findings or a representative survey of adherents.
metadata.phrase: A democratic society combining personal dignity, social responsibility and a market economy, with decisions made close to the communities affected.

sources.title: Resolutions adopted at the EPP Congress in Bucharest, 17–18 October 2012
The EPP’s path forward: a Europe of opportunity and strength
Carlo Invernizzi Accetti: Social Capitalism, chapter summary (not paywalled chapter)
Sicheres Zusammenleben, geordnete Migration: implemented measures and proposals distinguished

axes.brief: EPP democratic pluralism and rule of law, reinforced by Centesimus Annus 46, support accountable representative institutions.
axes.counterEvidence: Militant democracy can exclude unconstitutional parties by courts; that does not authorise incumbent discretion. Referendums and recalls are weaker inferences than elections.

answers.rationale: Elections confer public authority, not birth or expertise.
Expertise advises citizens but cannot replace their electoral mandate.
Equal personal dignity supports an inclusive adult franchise.
Executive authority remains subject to representative lawmaking.
Pluralism requires fair political competition.
Public responsibility requires opposition scrutiny of spending.
Constitutional legality needs courts able to restrain government.
Social partnership is not a trade-union monopoly on government.
Party exclusion requires independent constitutional procedure rather than leadership preference.
Popular participation is valuable but referendums must coexist with parliamentary deliberation and minority rights.
Subsidiarity and constitutional institutions reject sole personal authority.
Defined removal procedures protect accountable office.
Continuity cannot be a unilateral excuse to suspend elections.
Accountability supports recall while representative independence supports fixed terms.
Public office is entrusted and answerable.
Civilian constitutional rule precludes military self-authorisation.

axes.brief: Personal dignity limits coercion; the common good permits proportionate public safety powers under law.
axes.counterEvidence: The August 2026 German government page distinguishes enacted terrorism and policing laws from proposals. It illustrates stronger security policy; no single coalition is treated as the entire tradition.

answers.rationale: Personal autonomy and responsibility for health pull in different directions on drugs.
Judicially authorised serious-crime surveillance can protect the common good.
Peaceful protest merits protection despite limited inconvenience.
Criticism belongs to democratic freedom even when offensive.
Protection of life supports some health requirements but self-regarding coercion requires limits.
Indiscriminate years-long movement retention exceeds proportionate security.
Road safety can justify minimally intrusive sobriety checks.
A judicial finding of concrete danger can warrant preventive restrictions.
Pluralist civil liberty usually outweighs official moral disapproval.
Privacy favours anonymity while crime prevention supports limited identification duties.
Serious danger supports searches but absence of individual grounds weakens justification.
Credible disorder can justify proportionate restrictions subject to review.
The home requires legal protection with emergency exceptions.
Accountability generally supports disclosures exposing misconduct.
Protecting public security supports tighter limits than a violence-history check alone.
Indefinite detention without independent review violates rule of law.

axes.brief: The tradition combines inherited European cultural identity with pluralism, integration and individual dignity.
axes.counterEvidence: EPP diversity commitments counter a purely assimilationist reading. A common language does not entail suppressing minority identity.

answers.rationale: Shared civic-cultural commitments deserve weight when practices conflict.
Dignity and participation justify reasonable cultural accommodation.
Integration entails shared obligations without wholesale adoption of every custom.
A foreign identity can coexist with common civic membership.
A common public language facilitates social participation.
Recognition of original communities respects historical responsibility.
Stewardship gives inherited traditions special cultural attention.
Distinct identities should not automatically override shared civic life.
A workable common calendar can coexist with reasonable religious accommodations.
Pluralism permits several traditions within national identity.
Active integration and common participation are positively valued.
Accessibility supports some translations but not a universal signage rule.
Family socialisation should include shared membership alongside community ties.
Equal public rules generally outweigh a blanket clothing exemption.
Common institutions can encompass multiple cultural ways of life.
Integration should emphasise common civic practices without forced cultural erasure.

axes.brief: Managed migration coexists with asylum, family obligations and European freedom of movement.
axes.counterEvidence: Germany enacted a two-year pause in family reunification for subsidiary protection from 24 July 2025; this is narrower than all permanently settled migrants and is recorded as counter-evidence, not silently generalised.

answers.rationale: Capacity-based management is compatible with responsibility to receiving communities.
Mobility and dignity support admission but do not create an unrestricted settlement entitlement.
Family and refugee obligations preclude a skills-only rule.
Family unity normally supports reunification of settled residents.
Protection should not depend on marketable skills or cultural similarity.
Legal order supports removal after fair process rather than automatic regularisation.
Employers’ demand is not the only legitimate admission criterion.
Community capacity can justify moderated inflows.
Capacity management and family unity require exceptions rather than one rigid cap.
Lawful labour mobility is normally beneficial with safeguards.
Sponsorship may assist integration but cannot exclude protected humanitarian routes.
Education alone need not guarantee permanent residence.
Asylum obligations require protection beyond ordinary economic quotas.
Equal dignity weighs against cultural-origin preference.
Lawfully resident migrants should have social protection under fair eligibility rules.
Cultural diversity can benefit society but is not by itself an admission criterion.

axes.brief: Justified defence and alliance solidarity coexist with peace, proportionality and restraint.
axes.counterEvidence: The recent EPP commitment to a Defence Union and Ukraine support counters an assumption that Christian peace ethics imply unconditional pacifism.

answers.rationale: Defence of vital interests is legitimate only with necessity and just-war constraints.
Diplomacy normally precedes force.
Credible deterrence can require substantial defence expenditure.
Imminent attack can justify proportionate anticipatory defence.
Defence is central but narrowly justified collective humanitarian action may also be possible.
Defence duties are legitimate but neither male-only conscription nor universal service is indispensable.
Peace warrants compromise but not abandonment of essential rights.
Human responsibility for lethal decisions outweighs efficiency alone.
Territorial and allied defence should be the principal mission.
Duties to protect victims and allies rule out peace at any cost.
Alliance responsibilities can require deployable sustained forces.
Territorial claims alone do not justify initiating war.
Deterrence may support peace but coercive threats require strict justification.
Peace usually outweighs symbolic displays of resolve.
Necessary intelligence can support defensive security despite diplomatic costs.
Verified reciprocal arms reductions can strengthen peace.

axes.brief: European integration and shared institutions qualify national sovereignty; subsidiarity limits centralisation.
axes.counterEvidence: EPP support for common defence and trade does not imply that every international body should override rights or democratic consent.

answers.rationale: EU membership entails some lawful shared authority.
Agreed institutions can bind members despite a particular government’s objections.
Accepted international adjudication cannot routinely be displaced by domestic preference.
Durable alliances and integration are positive commitments.
Voluntary membership supports exit but existing legal obligations require orderly procedures.
International adjudication helps restrain abuses by officials.
Common responsibilities sometimes outweigh immediate national advantage.
Cross-border ecology requires shared authority.
A common European foreign policy is positively supported.
Human-rights obligations can require domestic legal change.
Shared European monetary institutions are compatible with the tradition.
Solidarity supports pooled resources for shared problems.
Common European border governance can be legitimate.
Common trade rules sustain the social market across borders.
European political integration is acceptable within subsidiarity.
Enforcing agreed rules can warrant costs to immediate national advantage.

axes.brief: Social-market private property is the default; public provision and ownership are legitimate when solidarity or strategic needs require them.
axes.counterEvidence: Accetti’s chapter summary identifies social capitalism, not wholesale socialism. Catholic social teaching also rejects property absolutism.

answers.rationale: General private enterprise is preferable to government ownership.
Essential networks may be public or regulated private providers according to effectiveness.
Subsidiarity favours private initiative when outcomes are comparable.
Routine competitive industries normally belong to private enterprise.
Health solidarity fixes access rather than requiring private facility ownership.
Shared rail infrastructure can justify public ownership as a natural network.
Lower contracting cost matters but social duties and accountability also determine service delivery.
Public development banks can complement private credit.
Non-strategic commercial holdings may appropriately be privatised.
Public housing can meet needs the market leaves unmet.
Effective regulation can make private strategic ownership acceptable.
Stewardship permits both public resource ownership and regulated private extraction.
Subsidiarity permits contracting where standards and accountability hold.
Strategic purpose can justify retention but not regardless of all costs.
Persistent failure can justify sale after protecting essential service obligations.
A public broadcaster can sustain shared civic information alongside private media.

axes.brief: Open competition and trade are preferred, with strategic resilience and fair-competition safeguards.
axes.counterEvidence: Current EPP calls to protect producers from unfair competition qualify its support for increased trade.

answers.rationale: Blanket tariffs undermine open competition.
Most barriers should fall within fair rules.
Local resilience can matter but procurement should generally reward value.
Firms should normally choose international suppliers within lawful safeguards.
Essential resilience can justify exceptions but blanket import restrictions are excessive.
Openness has benefits but reciprocal fair treatment also matters.
Temporary help can be justified when proportionate rather than permanent protection.
Equal market access is normally desirable under security review.
Farming resilience and open competition require a sector-specific balance.
Firms normally should adapt rather than depend on protection.
Proportionate response may defend fair rules but retaliation can escalate harm.
Equal taxation normally supports fair competition.
Countervailing measures can address demonstrably subsidised competition.
Tariff removal is desirable but strategic dependence requires safeguards.
Strategic screening can outweigh additional investment in sensitive sectors.
Cross-border digital commerce should normally remain open.

axes.brief: Market coordination, collective bargaining and entrepreneurial initiative coexist with social rules and strategic support.
axes.counterEvidence: The EPP’s contemporary industrial strategy is counter-evidence to laissez-faire; it does not establish routine compulsory output schedules.

answers.rationale: Enterprises generally decide output within social rules.
Compulsory sector-wide targets exceed ordinary social-market governance.
Prices normally communicate supply and demand.
Strategic investment policy is legitimate but comprehensive state direction is excessive.
Consumer demand normally guides commercial survival.
Essential affordability may justify intervention but sustained controls can restrict supply.
Competition requires ordinary freedom of market entry.
Development lending is legitimate but coercive credit allocation needs justification.
Capital movement is normally free under prudential safeguards.
Targeted support can address strategic or ecological public needs.
Monetary stability favours accountable common money over unregulated currency rivalry.
A wage floor can protect dignity where bargaining is insufficient.
Collective bargaining is a central social-partnership institution.
Democratic policy goals matter but monetary stability needs institutional restraint.
Property incentives and affordable shelter justify a conditional approach to rent rules.
Routine national direction of all production displaces subsidiarity and market signals.

axes.brief: Solidarity supports progressive contributions and adequate support; responsibility and incentives oppose unlimited equalisation.
axes.counterEvidence: Centesimus Annus criticises excessive bureaucratic welfare dependency while requiring support for genuine need.

answers.rationale: Excessive inequality threatens cohesion and warrants redistribution.
Social cohesion makes reducing inequality a legitimate fiscal aim.
Adequate minimum support can justify higher contributions.
A dignified floor is essential but full equalisation is not the objective.
Capacity to contribute supports progressive taxation.
Earned property and incentives matter alongside obligations to vulnerable households.
Intergenerational family provision and distributive fairness require balanced inheritance taxation.
Continuing need should not be abandoned merely because a clock expires.
Wealth contributions may be justified but property and investment constraints matter.
Support should meet genuine social need rather than be minimised for taxpayers alone.
Human dignity includes participation beyond bare subsistence.
Tax restraint and adequate benefits must be weighed together.
Earned-income supplements can reconcile work incentives and solidarity.
Equal nominal marginal rates need not satisfy ability-to-pay fairness.
Widespread property is valued but compulsory land transfer requires exceptional justification.
Social insurance and participation can justify support beyond destitution.

axes.brief: Christian inspiration and public religious participation are compatible with elected civil authority and religious freedom.
axes.counterEvidence: Theological inspiration does not establish religious courts or reserved clerical seats. National church-state arrangements vary.

answers.rationale: Civil law needs reasons accessible to a plural public even when Christians supply its inspiration.
Biblical teaching should inspire citizens rather than automatically constitute statutory law.
Elected civil authorities need no clerical permission.
Christian heritage may be acknowledged without establishing an exclusive state faith.
Religious understanding should respect pupils’ freedom of conscience.
Optional confessional instruction and plural choice differ from compulsory state conversion.
Civil institutions must retain legal authority.
Faith communities may be consulted but no privileged legislative veto follows.
Voluntary worship may appropriately accompany public occasions.
Social support for churches may serve community life but coercive evangelisation is excluded.
Historical religious symbols can coexist with equal citizenship in this tradition.
Inherited religious festivals may retain public recognition.
Office should depend on civil appointment or election rather than ordination.
Associational freedom supports relief but exclusive religious privilege needs justification.
Civil marriage should not require clerical permission.
Religious choices may be respected but civil rights and judicial jurisdiction must prevail.

axes.brief: Family continuity and inherited moral commitments are balanced with personal dignity and equal civil participation.
axes.counterEvidence: The Vatican text is more restrictive than some contemporary EPP members. The assessment models the stated Christian-personalist tradition, not every member’s sexuality policy.

answers.rationale: Customs may adapt but continuity and inherited obligations retain weight.
Established practices deserve a presumption of continuity.
All families merit dignity while the married-parent model retains special normative value.
Equal dignity qualifies inherited roles without denying differentiated family understandings.
This traditional Christian-personalist formulation treats marriage as a male-female institution.
Stable married-parent families receive particular encouragement.
Protection of unborn life opposes treating elective abortion as socially ordinary.
Parental responsibility gives families substantial authority over sexual education.
The scoped family ideal gives weight to a mother-father parenting model.
Modesty is valued but pluralist society permits diverse clothing conventions.
Respectful address matters alongside disagreement over particular identity conventions.
Intergenerational moral formation is a central family responsibility.
Equal dignity supports social acceptance of nontraditional occupational roles.
Gradual institutional change can protect trust and social cohesion.
Accurate teaching and respect for parents require age-appropriate plural provision.
Customs can have social meaning beyond immediate practical utility.

axes.brief: Technological development is desirable but constrained by dignity, stewardship and irreversible risks.
axes.counterEvidence: EPP advocacy of AI and biotechnology counters blanket technological conservatism; Catholic concern for human life constrains embryo enhancement.

answers.rationale: Development benefits require proportionate safeguards despite incomplete certainty.
Some risks warrant trials but a universal long-term-evidence rule can obstruct useful progress.
Substantial infrastructure benefits can justify limited habitat loss with mitigation.
Human dignity supports robust medical safety evidence.
Productivity improvements are acceptable with retraining and social protection.
Stewardship and public development both carry real obligations.
Novel food benefits and stewardship require case-specific evidence.
Healthy-person neural enhancement deserves demanding safety scrutiny.
Innovation and conservation should work together rather than give unproven solutions priority.
Poorly understood ecological effects justify assessment before major building.
Basic safety alone is inadequate for potentially irreversible neural enhancement.
Medical responsibility supports supervised validation across patient groups.
Instrumental enhancement of embryos conflicts with the scoped dignity-of-life ethic.
Stewardship supports evidence about ecosystem effects before wide release.
Human housing and transport needs can justify development with safeguards.
Irreversible harms merit strong evidence before deployment.

axes.brief: Subsidiarity assigns decisions to the lowest effective level while solidarity justifies national minimums and coordination.
axes.counterEvidence: European and national solidarity qualify local fiscal autonomy; subsidiarity is not unlimited secession.

answers.rationale: Subsidiarity protects regional competence within common constitutional rights.
Authority disputes should follow constitutional allocation rather than automatic national supremacy.
Community self-rule matters but secession also affects wider obligations and minorities.
Legitimate national programmes can override obstruction only within allocated competence.
Regional constitutional self-government exemplifies subsidiarity.
Local responsibility generally weighs against a single police command.
Local fiscal responsibility must coexist with interregional solidarity.
Education should leave significant room for regional and family institutions.
Regional tax discretion supports accountable local choice.
National minimum employment rights can prevent destructive competition.
Local institutional choices merit substantial autonomy within legal rights.
A national healthcare entitlement can sustain solidarity despite local delivery.
Indigenous local self-government can express subsidiarity and cultural dignity.
Some common tax rules protect solidarity against a race to the bottom.
Locally confined environmental decisions belong principally to the region.
A cross-regional disaster justifies coordination at the level capable of handling it.

axes.brief: Personalism treats people as embodied, socially formed and morally responsible; it does not reduce behaviour to genes or social engineering.
axes.counterEvidence: Theological human nature is not biological heritability. Neutral judgements explicitly balance embodied capacities with formation; no empirical gene-share is claimed.

answers.rationale: Personalism recognises social formation and embodied dispositions without making either universally primary.
Equal dignity rejects political ranking but supplies no warranted cross-national IQ causal priority.
Embodied sexual difference and social roles both matter in this anthropology.
Stress involves bodily vulnerability and lived circumstances rather than one ideological master cause.
Education shapes interests while individual capacities and inclinations remain real.
Responsible agency involves temperament as well as learning in risky choices.
Solidarity is cultivated but also understood as part of relational human nature.
Empathy involves personal formation and embodied capacities together.
Attention combines personal capacities with educational and social conditions.
Conscience is formed culturally while moral responsibility is not reduced to conditioning.
Fear is embodied and learned; personalism does not rank the two generally.
Stable dispositions and upbringing both belong in the personalist account.
Bodily attraction and cultural formation are both recognised without a fixed ratio.
Personalist anthropology recognises social conditions and embodied human capacities; equal dignity alone does not establish which explains racial differences in violent offending more.
Moral education and personal responsibility count against inherited racial accounts of self-control.

The social-market commitment to fair treatment and family responsibilities recognises institutional barriers and unpaid care; it therefore resists explaining the pay gap mainly by sex differences in productive contribution.

review.notes: Read all 240 answers against the current question wording and checked values, rationales, cited source IDs and axis distinctions. Checked EPP doctrine and current programme against Centesimus Annus and the available Cambridge chapter summary (not its inaccessible full chapter). Verified the German government security page and its narrow subsidiary-protection family-reunification suspension, not a general ban on permanent migrants. Replaced the Culture14 moral-equality inference with an explicit mixed anthropology judgement; Culture16 now addresses economic contribution and socially structured work. Retained family policy and subsidiarity qualifications. All answers remain labelled inferred: these are scoped representative models, not claimed questionnaire responses or empirical measurements of adherents. Review used no target scores or similarity tuning. Similarity audit remains the catalogue coordinator’s separate step.
